title: Speaking the Trade
text:
Every profession develops a specialised vocabulary, and its jargon can be both a precise tool and a barrier. Surgeons speak of 'anastomosis' when they mean a surgical join between two vessels, a term that would puzzle most patients. Within a single hospital, however, such words allow staff to communicate quickly and avoid dangerous ambiguity. Jargon becomes a problem only when it excludes people who need the information most.

Lawyers, engineers, and software developers face the same tension. A contract may rely on terms such as 'indemnity' or 'consideration', which carry legal meanings far narrower than their everyday senses. Experts who explain their field to outsiders must therefore translate their terminology into plain language. The best communicators do not abandon technical words; they define them carefully and then use them consistently.

questions.text: According to the passage, what does 'anastomosis' refer to?
options: A surgical join between two vessels
A type of patient consent form
A method of measuring blood pressure
A common word for a hospital ward

questions.text: What do experts need to do when explaining their field to outsiders?
options: Translate their terminology into plain language
Stop using any technical words at all
Ask outsiders to learn the jargon first
Use only words with the same everyday meaning

questions.text: Why might jargon be useful inside a single hospital?
options: It lets staff communicate quickly and avoid dangerous ambiguity
It prevents staff from speaking with each other at all
It makes patients feel more relaxed about their treatment
It replaces the need for any written records

questions.text: What does the passage imply about the best communicators in technical fields?
options: They define technical terms carefully and use them consistently
They avoid technical words to keep their audience comfortable
They change the meaning of key terms for each new audience
They rely on everyday words because specialist words are unreliable

vocabulary.definition: specialised words used by a particular group, often hard for outsiders to understand
the quality of having more than one possible meaning
a legal promise to protect someone against loss or harm
in a way that is always the same, without changes

paragraph_translations: Her meslek, kendine özgü bir sözcük dağarcığı geliştirir ve bu meslek dili hem kesin bir araç hem de bir engel olabilir. Cerrahlar, iki damar arasındaki cerrahi birleşmeyi kastettiklerinde 'anastomosis' sözcüğünden söz eder; bu terim çoğu hastayı şaşırtır. Ancak tek bir hastanenin içinde bu tür sözcükler personelin hızlı iletişim kurmasını ve tehlikeli belirsizlikten kaçınmasını sağlar. Meslek dili ancak en çok bilgiye ihtiyaç duyan insanları dışladığında bir soruna dönüşür.

Avukatlar, mühendisler ve yazılım geliştiriciler de aynı gerilimle karşı karşıyadır. Bir sözleşme, günlük anlamlarından çok daha dar hukuki anlamlar taşıyan 'indemnity' ya da 'consideration' gibi terimlere dayanabilir. Bu nedenle alanını dışarıdakilere anlatan uzmanlar, terminolojilerini sade bir dile çevirmelidir. En iyi iletişimciler teknik sözcükleri terk etmez; onları dikkatle tanımlar ve sonra tutarlı biçimde kullanır.
